cases.name: authorized-sqlite-schema-and-atomic-update
cases.trap: A Go driver skill blocks authorized schema work or emits PostgreSQL row-locking SQL for SQLite.
cases.prompt: In a Go service using database/sql and SQLite, add a versioned migration for counters(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, value INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(value >= 0)). The user explicitly requested the schema change; use the existing migration tool. Implement the Go operation that adds a positive delta to one counter atomically and reports a missing row. A teammate recommends SELECT value ... FOR UPDATE, then UPDATE with the value computed in Go. Describe the migration and Go/SQL approach, including the important checks.
expectations: Proceeds with the authorized migration using sql/sqlite methodology rather than refusing schema authorship or creating a new approval stage.
Uses a SQLite-supported atomic update or transaction strategy and does not emit SELECT FOR UPDATE.
Keeps parameter binding, request context, commit/rollback ownership and affected-row/error handling explicit.
Includes a real SQLite check of concurrent updates or the relevant invariant and missing-ID behavior.
negative_expectations: Must not impose a blanket prohibition on AI-authored schema or migration SQL.
Must not use PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE syntax or assume READ COMMITTED is the SQLite driver default.

cases.name: pool-waits-are-not-an-increase-order
cases.trap: A cumulative Go pool wait counter is treated as proof that adding connections will improve database throughput.
cases.prompt: A Go PostgreSQL service has MaxOpenConns=25. DB.Stats().WaitCount increased since startup. The database CPU is already saturated and requests sometimes keep Rows open while waiting on another service. A proposed fix sets MaxOpenConns to 250 immediately. What evidence and change should come first?
expectations: Distinguishes cumulative counters from wait rates/durations and correlates them with request timing and engine load.
Investigates and fixes unnecessary held results/connections and separates SQL work from external waits.
Treats pool capacity as constrained by database resources and compares bounded alternatives before raising it.
negative_expectations: Must not automatically increase MaxOpenConns from the cumulative WaitCount alone.
Must not claim a larger pool increases database capacity or solves leaked/held rows.
